disclaimer: This ruleset is for general guidance only and is not a medical diagnosis. If symptoms are severe or worsening, seek in-person care. For life-threatening symptoms, call local emergency services immediately.

rules.condition: Possible stroke or serious neurologic emergency
rules.advice: Seek emergency care now. Do not drive yourself if symptoms are significant; call emergency services.
followup_questions: When did these symptoms start (exact time)?
Is one side of the body weaker than the other?
Any severe headache, vision loss, or trouble walking?

rules.advice: Seek emergency care now. If symptoms are severe (pressure/tightness, trouble breathing, fainting), call emergency services immediately.
followup_questions: Is the chest pain pressure/tightness, and does it spread to arm/jaw/back?
Do you have shortness of breath at rest, sweating, or fainting?
How long has this been happening?

rules.advice: Seek emergency care now. Call emergency services if you are struggling to breathe, turning blue, or unable to speak in full sentences.
followup_questions: Are you able to speak full sentences?
Any swelling of lips/tongue or recent allergen exposure?
Any known asthma/COPD or inhaler use?

rules.advice: Seek emergency care now. Call emergency services if there is throat/tongue swelling, wheezing, or trouble breathing.
followup_questions: Did symptoms start after food/medicine/insect sting?
Is there swelling of lips/tongue or difficulty swallowing?
Any dizziness or fainting?

rules.advice: Seek urgent emergency evaluation now, especially if headache is sudden and severe, with confusion, seizure, neck stiffness, or vision changes.
followup_questions: Did the headache start suddenly (seconds to minutes)?
Any fever, neck stiffness, confusion, weakness, or vision changes?
Any recent head injury?

rules.condition: Fever with possible dehydration or systemic illness
rules.advice: Seek same-day medical care. If there is confusion, fainting, severe weakness, or worsening symptoms, go to urgent care or emergency care now.
followup_questions: What is the highest temperature you measured (and how)?
How long has the fever lasted?
Are you able to keep fluids down and urinate normally?

rules.condition: Viral upper respiratory infection (possible cold/flu-like illness)
rules.advice: Rest, drink fluids, and monitor symptoms. Seek medical care sooner if breathing worsens, fever is very high or persistent, you feel faint/confused, or symptoms worsen instead of improving.
followup_questions: How many days have symptoms been present?
Any shortness of breath at rest or chest pain?
Any high-risk conditions (pregnancy, immune problems, chronic lung/heart disease)?

rules.condition: Possible lower respiratory infection (needs clinical assessment)
rules.advice: Seek same-day medical evaluation, especially if breathing is difficult, chest pain occurs, or fever is high/persistent.
followup_questions: Do you have shortness of breath at rest or chest pain when breathing?
How high is the fever and for how many days?
Any known lung disease or low oxygen readings?

rules.advice: Avoid known triggers when possible and monitor symptoms. Seek medical care if symptoms are severe, recurrent, or associated with wheezing, facial swelling, or trouble breathing.
followup_questions: Do symptoms worsen in certain environments (dust/pollen/pets)?
Any wheezing or shortness of breath?
Any fever or thick, foul-smelling nasal discharge?

rules.advice: If you have severe breathing trouble, blue lips, or cannot speak in full sentences, seek emergency care now. Otherwise, arrange same-day medical evaluation if wheezing persists or is worsening.
followup_questions: Do you have a history of asthma or inhaler use?
Are you short of breath at rest or waking at night due to symptoms?
Any known trigger (exercise, infection, smoke, allergens)?

rules.condition: Abdominal pain with possible red flags
rules.advice: Seek urgent medical evaluation today. Go to emergency care if pain is severe, you faint, there is vomiting blood/black stools, or symptoms worsen rapidly.
followup_questions: Where is the pain located (right/left, upper/lower)?
Any vomiting, black stools, or blood in vomit/stool?
Any pregnancy possibility, or recent surgery?

rules.advice: Focus on hydration and monitor. Seek medical care if you cannot keep fluids down, have signs of dehydration, severe abdominal pain, blood in stool/vomit, high or persistent fever, or symptoms last more than a few days.
followup_questions: How many times in the last 24 hours have you vomited/had diarrhea?
Any blood in stool or black stool?
Are you able to keep fluids down and urinate normally?

rules.advice: Seek urgent in-person evaluation today. Go to emergency care if pain is severe, worsening, or associated with fainting or inability to keep fluids down.
followup_questions: Is the pain mainly in the right lower abdomen, and is it worsening?
Any fever, vomiting, or loss of appetite?
Does movement/coughing make the pain worse?

rules.condition: Headache pattern consistent with migraine (needs confirmation)
rules.advice: If this is a new or different headache, or you have red-flag symptoms (sudden severe onset, weakness, confusion, fever/neck stiffness, vision loss), seek urgent care. Otherwise, consider a routine clinician visit if headaches recur or disrupt daily life.
followup_questions: Is this headache similar to previous headaches you've had?
Any weakness, confusion, fainting, fever/neck stiffness, or vision changes?
How often do headaches occur and how long do they last?

rules.advice: Monitor symptoms and consider routine evaluation if headaches are frequent, worsening, or new. Seek urgent care for red flags (sudden severe headache, neurologic symptoms, fever/neck stiffness, fainting).
followup_questions: Any recent sleep deprivation, stress, or screen strain?
Any nausea, light sensitivity, or neurologic symptoms?
How many days per month do headaches occur?

rules.advice: Arrange same-day or next-day medical evaluation for testing and treatment. Seek urgent care sooner if you have fever, back/flank pain, vomiting, or you are pregnant.
followup_questions: Any fever, chills, nausea/vomiting, or back/flank pain?
Any blood in urine?
Are you pregnant or immunocompromised?

rules.advice: Seek urgent medical evaluation today, especially if fever with flank/back pain, nausea/vomiting, or worsening symptoms.
followup_questions: Any burning urination or frequent urination?
Any nausea/vomiting?
How high is the fever?

rules.condition: Eye irritation or conjunctivitis pattern (needs confirmation)
rules.advice: Avoid touching/rubbing eyes and monitor symptoms. Seek urgent eye care if you have severe eye pain, light sensitivity, sudden vision changes, or if you wear contact lenses with redness/pain.
followup_questions: Any severe pain, light sensitivity, or vision changes?
Do you wear contact lenses?
Is there thick discharge or both eyes affected?

rules.condition: Back pain pattern consistent with strain (needs monitoring)
rules.advice: Seek urgent care if you have weakness, numbness in the groin/saddle area, or loss of bladder/bowel control. Otherwise, arrange routine evaluation if pain is severe, persistent, or associated with fever, trauma, or unexplained weight loss.
followup_questions: Any leg weakness, numbness, or changes in bladder/bowel control?
Any recent injury/trauma?
How long has the pain lasted and is it improving?

rules.condition: Back pain with neurologic red flags
rules.advice: Seek urgent emergency evaluation now, especially with bladder/bowel control problems, groin numbness, or leg weakness.
followup_questions: Any new bladder/bowel control problems?
Any worsening leg weakness or numbness?
Any recent injury?

rules.advice: Arrange a routine evaluation if pain/swelling persists, is recurrent, or limits function. Seek urgent care if there is fever with a hot swollen joint, inability to bear weight, or recent injury with deformity.
followup_questions: Is the joint hot, very swollen, or associated with fever?
Was there an injury or inability to bear weight?
How long has the pain been present?

rules.condition: Hot/swollen joint with fever (needs urgent evaluation)
rules.advice: Seek urgent medical evaluation today. A hot, swollen joint with fever can be serious and needs in-person assessment.
followup_questions: Which joint is affected and is it hot to touch?
Do you have fever or feel unwell?
Any recent injury or infection?

rules.advice: Monitor the rash. Seek urgent care if rash is rapidly spreading, associated with fever, severe pain, blistering, facial swelling, or any breathing trouble.
followup_questions: Any fever, blistering, or severe pain?
Any new medication, food, or insect bite exposure?
Is there facial swelling or any breathing trouble?

rules.advice: Seek same-day medical care if you cannot keep fluids down or show signs of dehydration (very little urination, dizziness when standing, severe weakness).
followup_questions: How long has vomiting been happening and how frequent?
Any blood in vomit or severe abdominal pain?
Are you able to urinate normally?

rules.advice: Seek urgent medical evaluation, especially if fainting occurred with chest pain, shortness of breath, severe bleeding, or neurologic symptoms.
followup_questions: Did you fully lose consciousness, and for how long?
Any chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations?
Any injury from the fall?

rules.condition: Sore throat (may need testing depending on symptoms)
rules.advice: Arrange a clinician visit if sore throat is severe, lasts more than a few days, or occurs with high fever, difficulty swallowing, or dehydration. Seek urgent care for trouble breathing, drooling, or inability to swallow fluids.
followup_questions: Any trouble breathing, drooling, or inability to swallow fluids?
Do you have cough or runny nose (viral signs) versus isolated sore throat?
How many days have symptoms lasted?

rules.advice: Arrange a routine clinician visit if pain is significant or persistent, or if there is fever, discharge, or hearing loss. Seek urgent care for severe pain, swelling behind the ear, or neurologic symptoms.
followup_questions: Any fever, ear discharge, or hearing loss?
Is there pain when pulling the outer ear?
How long has the ear pain been present?

rules.condition: Possible skin infection (needs assessment if worsening)
rules.advice: Arrange a clinician visit if redness is spreading, there is fever, severe pain, or pus/abscess. Seek urgent care if you feel very unwell or the area is rapidly worsening.
followup_questions: Is the redness spreading or very painful?
Any fever or chills?
Any diabetes or immune system problems?

rules.advice: I can help with general guidance, but I need more details. If symptoms are severe, worsening, or you are worried, seek in-person medical care.
followup_questions: What are your main symptoms (top 2–3) and how long have they been present?
How severe is it (mild/moderate/severe) and is it getting worse?
Any red flags like chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting, confusion, severe dehydration, or weakness on one side?
